rationale: Round-6 zero-ask regression check of b98d06c2 under the grounding lens, both assigned evidence claims verified — one against the installed documentation, one by lab. (1) DOC CLAIM VERIFIED VERBATIM: installed git is 2.51.2, and git-update-ref(1) states (man page, TRANSACTIONS section): 'If all <ref>s can be locked with matching <old-oid>s simultaneously, all modifications are performed. Otherwise, no modifications are performed. Note that while each individual <ref> is updated or deleted atomically, a concurrent reader may still see a subset of the modifications.' The plan quotes the subset sentence exactly, and the author's interpretation is the sound reading of the pair: the transaction gives all-or-nothing DECISION semantics at lock time (which is precisely what my round-5 lab demonstrated — prepare-abort on expected-old mismatch), while installation is per-ref, so a crash mid-commit can leave one ref installed. The replacement of the two-ref transaction is therefore a genuine deepening, not a walk-back: my round-5 lab evidence proved the decision property and could not have probed the crash-installation window, and the plan now records exactly that evidence-grade distinction ('authoritative documentation + documented per-ref installation order, NOT a lab-reproduced crash window') — honest grading, and replacement-over-patching is the right shape since the write-ahead design needs no multi-ref atomicity at all and drops the version floor to plain plumbing. (2) WRITE-AHEAD MECHANICS VERIFIED BY LAB (fresh scratch repo, files backend): the marker commit's first parent encodes the predecessor exactly as claimed (C built -p A gives marker^ == A; D built -p C gives marker^ == C); the crash-window state tip == marker^ is detectable and the finish-advance ('expected-old = tip') installs cleanly; the structural kind test discriminates correctly — C's marker-vs-marker^ diff was exactly the non-artifact path (f.txt, NOT artifact-confined → classified C) while D's was exactly the named artifact (artifact.jsonl only → classified D, predecessor == C); and a foreign tip ∉ {M*, M*^} is detected. All three re-entry legs of the discriminator are real states I constructed and probed. (3) The protocol text is consistent across the protocol paragraph, bead 6, and the ADR-0041 draft description in write-ahead terms, and my round-5 minor finding R2-5-3 (no index refresh after S) is ADDRESSED by this commit's G2 S-stage exit contract, which pins exactly the refresh-to-D plus dirt classification plus the named-paths refusal before any worktree-removing path — a stronger resolution than my one-line suggestion, closing the silent-interval-edit-loss hole R6 found alongside it. ONE minor precision residual, non-blocking: the structural kind test ('diff M* vs M*^ confined to the named artifact → D, else C') is vacuously artifact-confined when the first-parent diff is EMPTY. This can only bite if the tool ever publishes a marker for an empty C (worktree tree == tip tree at snapshot) or an empty D (refreshed blob == tip blob); today's flow only commits when there is something to commit, and S is presumably skipped when the artifact is unchanged, but the plan does not explicitly pin the stage-skip conditions that make the discriminator total. One sentence ('M is skipped when T equals the tip tree; S is skipped when the refreshed blob equals the tip blob — hence every published marker has a nonempty first-parent diff') would close it. Recording for fold-in; it does not warrant a round.

Only reachable if the tool publishes a marker for an empty C (T == tip tree) or empty D (refreshed blob == tip blob) — states the flow presumably skips, but the skip is unstated.
